svg.aria-label: A one-page design for the Windmill Yard: fourteen events in one medium location, seven of them a fixed chain and seven free to fire in any order, drawn so the difference is visible.
svg.title: Windmill Yard, fourteen events
svg.desc: Level sheet archetype. Sequenced events are navy circles joined by a chain; free events are gold diamonds with no connections. One free event is gated, and the gate is drawn rather than described.

g.inkscape:label: 10 Title
g.text: One medium location. Fourteen events, and which of them have an order.
north gate, out to The Split

g.inkscape:label: 50 Lists
g.text: THE CHAIN · must happen in order
Step through the gate. The yard is quiet.
The sails stop. Wind drops to zero.
Fetch the crank from the grain store.
North gate opens. You may leave.
FREE · any time, any order, or never
Feed the goats. They follow you after.
Knock the bale stack down. Pure physics.
Ring the bell. The goats come running.
Read the notice board. Names the valley.
Wake the dog under the cart.
Wind the well bucket up. Something in it.
free, but gated. The gate is drawn

g.inkscape:label: 60 Note
g.text: WHY SEQUENCED AND FREE ARE DRAWN DIFFERENTLY
Most level documents list events and leave the ordering in prose, so the reader has to hold the whole
dependency graph in their head. Here the chain IS a chain: if a marker has a line into it, something must
happen first. If it has no line, it can fire whenever, in any order, or never at all.
The useful consequence: seven of the fourteen can be cut without touching the chain.
A drawing that makes cuttable content obvious is worth more at a scope meeting than a list ever is.
Events 2 and 6 set WindSystem strength to 0
and back up. The whole yard reacts: plants,
cloth, the vane. One value, a location-wide beat.
Every event here is an ActionTriggerComponent.
No scripting needed anywhere on this sheet.

g.inkscape:label: 99 Footer
g.text: Landmark 3 of Kettle Hollow. Roughly six minutes of the twenty-four, and the first place the player is left alone with a problem.
